signals.text: The drama department fosters confidence, determination, resilience, and open-mindedness, preparing students for any future career and providing high-quality training for aspiring performers, directors, producers, and writers.

Therefore, our team of expert staff have created a broad, balanced and exciting curriculum which is enhanced by a range of enrichment and extra-curricular experiences which take our students beyond the classroom, broadening their horizons.
At EKC Sheppey Secondary, we offer a range of clubs and extra-curricular activities throughout Year 7 to 11.

Welcome to EKC Sheppey SecondaryWhere belonging meets brilliance
EKC Sheppey Secondary opened its doors in September 2024, ready to nurture every student’s unique spark. Our experienced team, rooted in the community and deeply invested in its success, is here to enable your child to achieve their ambitions. Whether academic or professional specialism, further study or a chosen career, our curriculum is rich, rigorous and relevant and there’s a pathway for everyone.
We’re here to champion mastery (not just milestones); we’ll fuel aspiration and achievement and cheer students on every step of the way. We’re not just opening a school, but forging a learning community where every student thrives… where belonging meets brilliance.
January LormanHeadteacher

Art & Creative
Art and Design
Our art rooms are a space for creative expression, where students can freely develop their ideas and thoughts. Learning through and about the arts enriches the school experience and prepares students for life beyond. Our aim is to engage, inspire, and challenge pupils, fostering resilience, confidence, and independence, and equipping them with skills to invent and create.
Creative
In Creative, learning involves developing media skills through practical projects alongside theory work, providing a comprehensive understanding of the industry. Units cover pre-production techniques, communication skills for creative media production, research techniques, and film and video editing techniques. A key component of the course is building your portfolio, which showcases your practical skills and actual media products, enabling progression into your desired subject area within the industry.

Careers
At EKCSS, our careers programme is delivered in a number of exciting ways throughout each year group.
Careers Advice and Guidance
Our aim is to fully prepare all of our students with the competencies they will need to succeed in the 21st Century world. Our curriculum has clear, signposted links with careers to enable all learners to identify their next steps to progress into their bright futures.
In addition to this, students are provided with personalised advice and guidance to ensure that they studying the qualifications to be able to enter into either higher education or the working world with all the skills they need.
To view our current Year 9 Options Booklet please click here
Our Careers Lead is Miss Ginny Weymouth, and our Careers Advisor is Mr Ben Lasnig.
If you require any further information about careers at EKCSS, please click here to contact Mr Lasnig.

Our Parents
Our parents, carers and families are integral to our community. We are delighted to have had their support throughout our first year of opening. Our parents have donated to our causes, demonstrated unprecedented attendance at our events and speak highly of the first class education their young people have access to.

Science
Science education helps students understand how and why the world works, from human anatomy to complex systems. It reveals the mechanisms behind natural phenomena and technological advancements, fostering a deeper knowledge of their surroundings.

Curriculum
At EKC Sheppey Secondary, we want all students to value their education and recognise the vital role that it will play in ensuring a successful and happy future. We know the importance of your children having a range of skills to guide them into their bright futures. English
English empowers students to become effective communicators. By exploring diverse texts and developing strong reading, writing, spelling, punctuation, and grammar skills, students gain a deeper understanding of themselves and the interconnected world. Geography explores the relationships between people and their environments, examining both Earth's physical properties and human societies. Students learn how human culture interacts with nature and how locations impact individuals, developing into confident, independent, and reflective enquirers.

It also develops critical thinking, analysis, evaluation, reading, and writing skills essential for life.

Mathematics is a creative and powerful discipline fundamental to understanding our world. It provides solutions to complex problems and is essential for daily life, science, technology, engineering, and financial literacy. A high-quality mathematics education fosters logical reasoning, appreciation for the subject's beauty, and a lifelong love of learning.

We want them to be kind, motivated, resilient, and ready for their next step, potentially becoming future leaders so that they, too, can impact change for the better within our community and the wider world.
Character Education
Our Character Education curriculum develops independent students who are aware and confident in keeping themselves healthy and safe, now and in the future. It prepares them for life beyond school by exploring current issues, promoting respectful relationships, and appreciating diverse worldviews, incorporating statutory guidance on Religious Education and PSHE.
PHSE
PSHE education is a vital part of the curriculum, dedicated to equipping students with the essential knowledge, understanding, skills, and attributes they need to manage their lives successfully, both now and in the future. At its heart, PSHE aims to empower students to become healthy, safe, independent, and responsible members of society. We deliver PHSE through our Character Education, Life Skills and daily mentoring sessions.

As part of our extensive personal development program and our commitment to both local and global communities, our students actively participate in social action projects throughout the year. Participating in clubs and extracurricular activities offers significant benefits that extend beyond the classroom. They also foster personal growth by boosting confidence, allowing individuals to explore new interests, and providing a healthy outlet for stress. Socially, these groups are excellent for building new friendships and developing key skills like communication and teamwork.
At EKC Sheppey Secondary, we offer a range of clubs and extra-curricular activities throughout Year 7 to 11. To find out more, please check our calendar.
Right to Withdraw
As laid out by the Department for Education, parents and carers have the right to withdraw their children from Sex Education, covered as part of the Personal Development curriculum. Parents may chose to withdraw their child from all parts of the Sex Education curriculum, or only some sections for example contraception. This is possible up to and until three terms before your child turns 16. After that point, if your child wishes to receive Sex Education rather than be withdrawn, the school will make arrangements to provide your child with Sex Education during one of these terms.
Parents and carers also have the right to request that their child is withdrawn from Religious Education. This, again, can be from part or all of the curriculum.
If you wish to withdraw your child from Sex Education or from Religious Education, this should be communicated to the Headteacher in writing. This is possible via the main school office.
There is no right to withdraw for Relationships Education or Health Education.
